Write one python policy that decides how to investigate.

Interface: exactly one module-level function STEP(view, state).
The view holds task_content, observations, open_questions,
last_result, eligible_methods, remaining and contract_versions.
Return exactly {"action": <action>, "state": <object>}.
Action kinds: diagnose, construct_method, use_method, request_model, propose_revision, stop.
An action holds kind, target, inputs, evidence_refs and
requested_resources; shapes are strict.
Entry: STEP(view, state) with the two parameters must be named view and state, no *args, **kwargs, or keyword-only parameters.
The word import anywhere in the entry source fails validation,
so use no imports, no dunder access, no IO. Precisely: import statements fail validation; attribute access starting with a single underscore and variable names starting with a double underscore fail validation; calls to __import__,breakpoint,compile,delattr,dir,eval,exec,exit,getattr,globals,help,input,locals,memoryview,open,quit,setattr,type,vars fail validation.
Source must be non-empty python source that parses with exactly one module-level function carrying the entry name.
State is bounded JSON: at most 4096 bytes; larger states fail.
Reply with exactly one JSON object and nothing else, shaped {"entry": "<complete python source>", "notes": "<sentence>"}.
